sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Operations in Customs Free Trade Zones

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic commercial law tradition; unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–BLEU (Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union) Agreement on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (1986, in force)
Luxembourg–Hong Kong Double Taxation Agreement (2016, in force)
Luxembourg–Singapore Double Taxation Agreement (as amended by protocol, in force)
Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol, in force)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; ratification pending, not yet in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme; Loi modifiée du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); Loi du 25 mars 2020 portant transposition de la directive (UE) 2018/843; Règlement CSSF n° 12-02 du 14 décembre 2012 relatif à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 23 juillet 2016 ayant introduit la société en commandite spéciale, modifiant la loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales; Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés et la comptabilité des entreprises.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (post-CJEU C-37/20 WM and Sovim reform: Luxembourg RBE no longer grants unrestricted public access; access restricted to competent authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), obliged entities performing AML/KYC, and private persons demonstrating a legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade/commercial registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin (e.g., Luxembourg Business Registers; State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or provincial counterpart in China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China acceded to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention effective 7 November 2023; consular legalization abolished for Chinese public documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) authorizing the signatory to execute the partnership deed and RCS filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the jurisdiction of the grantor (shareholder/UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille + sworn translation into French/German/English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner, and of the general partner (major physical person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport-issuing authority / municipal civil registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy + Hague Apostille (if originating outside EU)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth / source-of-funds declaration for each material contributor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Settlement or private bank maintaining the client relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-confirmed letter; apostille required only if bank statement is elevated to notarized evidence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence and current directorship/partners of the corporate general partner (if SCSp is fronted by a Luxembourg or foreign corporate GP)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) or equivalent foreign registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory two-tier screening of all UBOs, general partners, directors, authorized signatories and commercial counterparties against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (EU sanctions map), (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists, (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and (iv) Luxembourg national freezing measures and CSSF PEP registries. Screening must be executed (a) at onboarding before the notarial deed, (b) re-run within 24 hours prior to signing the acte constitutif, and (c) continuously during the client relationship with a full refresh at least every 12 months or upon any material change. PEP classification covers family members and close associates under Article 3(6) of the amended Law of 12 November 2004; enhanced due diligence applies given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML risk tier of the bonded warehouse activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) central electronic platform (www.lbr.lu), including the e-filing module and the name register (Registre des noms); publications are made in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be renderable in Latin script; French, German, Luxembourgish and English tokens are accepted. Non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese) require a scientific transliteration (pinyin or equivalent) and a sworn translation of the meaning; the Latin-script transliteration constitutes the sole official corporate name in the RCS. The statutory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' must appear in the legal name of the partnership under the amended Law of 10 August 1915, and must not create confusion with any existing RCS-registered entity or protected name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / bancaire (requires CSSF prior authorization under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector)
Assurance / Insurance / réassurance (requires Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) prior authorization)
État / national / gouvernemental / officiel (implies public status; requires ministerial authorization)
Chambre de commerce / Bourse / LuxSE (requires institutional or stock exchange operator consent)
Fonds / SICAV / SICAR / SIF / placement collectif (requires CSSF product and sector authorization)
Université / école / institut de formation (requires Ministry of Education approval)

Termes évoquant le port franc, entrepôt douanier, zone franche (customs/free-zone tokens such as 'bonded', 'port franc', 'entrepôt douanier') requiring prior customs concession approval from the Administration des douanes et accises
Any token identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS name, trademark, or international non-proprietary name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS rejection or confusion notice, the applicant may: (i) resubmit the name reservation with a modified token at no additional statutory fee; (ii) file a written re-examination request with the LBR within 15 days of rejection; and (iii) if the rejection is maintained, file a petition (requête) with the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre commerciale) within 2 months of notification, under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS, seeking an order to register or reserve the name. Parallel remedial option: obtain a non-confusion certificate from a Luxembourg notary where the alleged conflict is merely phonetic. A reserved name which remains unused at expiry of the 90-day window is released; re-reservation is permitted for a further 90-day period if no third-party priority has intervened.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual/domiciliation-only office is legally acceptable for the SCSp itself as the statutory seat (siège statutaire), provided the registered address is maintained with a licensed fiduciary, support services provider (PFS/SPS), or authorized legal professional in Luxembourg. However, for the licensed bonded warehouse business (ISIC 5210, NAICS 493110), virtual substance is insufficient: customs authorities require a physically occupied, customs-approved storage facility (bonded depot) within a free trade zone in Luxembourg, with identifiable personnel, operational records and customs-controlled access; without such physical premises the customs authorisation under Union Customs Code Article 211 cannot be obtained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: (i) registered-office address verification by the RCS or AEDT — approximately 35% probability within the first 12 months; (ii) unannounced customs physical audits and stock/bond verifications by the Administration des douanes et accises under UCC risk-management rules — approximately 85% probability within the first 12 months of operation for a newly licensed bonded warehouse operator; (iii) CSSF or CRF supervisory/AML on-site visit if the SCSp is linked to regulated fund activity — approximately 25% probability within 24 months. Statistical basis: risk-tiering of customs excise and free-zone regimes as Medium_Risk_Enhanced.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS fee schedule (tarif RCS) under the amended Law of 19 December 2002

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notarial deed (acte constitutif) of the SCSp, including statutory minutes and legal-form compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary in the district of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 December 1991 on notarial tariffs, minimum scale applicable to partnerships with no minimum capital (SCSp has no statutory minimum capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration (dossier d'inscription) of the SCSp
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS filing fee (EUR 75 plus applicable VAT) per RCS fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic publication of the constitutional deed in RESA
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee for RESA publication under the Law of 23 June 2016

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RBE) initial filing and data verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee nominal; includes notarial administrative handling benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization bundle for foreign constitutional documents, powers of attorney and KYC records

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille fee schedule of the source state plus professional courier and agency handling benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (Chinese/French/English or German) of constitutional and KYC documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) on the Luxembourg list
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing court-approved translator tariff in Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service (year one)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary or support services provider (PFS/SPS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for domiciliation of SCSp vehicles (EUR 3,000–EUR 4,500 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC client file production, UBO analysis, PEP and sanctions screening, compliance sign-off
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for compliance services under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customs bonded warehouse authorisation application (Union Customs Code Article 211) and free-zone license coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs) via instructed customs agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customs application fee nominal; professional customs agent benchmark fee for UCC bonded warehouse and free-zone authorization files

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee nil; professional processing benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales); SCSp provisions at Articles 102-1 to 102-39; formation, publicity and registration at Articles 12, 27 to 33 and 49
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (contrat de société / statuts) executed by written deed or notarial act and registered with the RCS, followed by publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an SCSp; partners freely fix contributions in the partnership agreement. Any contractually agreed capital must be fully paid per the agreement and, where required by the drafting parties, held in a blocked/escrow bank account until RCS registration; execution is by private written deed except for contributions of immovable property or real rights therein, which require a notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner approves the draft partnership agreement and directs that it be executed and filed with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at the duly-consented address in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and that the day-to-day manager named in the filing be appointed with signatory powers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the escrowed capital contribution account be opened and that funds be released only upon RCS registration. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the managers execute the EORI and customs bonded warehouse applications, environmental clearances, and initial VAT registration filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and negative certificate procurement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name-availability request through the eJustice portal and obtain the negative certificate certifying that the proposed SCSp name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg entity or trade name. Verify compatibility with the Luxembourg Law of 17 March 2014 on trade names.
required_dossiers: Copy of identification of each requesting partner
Power of attorney if lodged by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a renewed request with alternative names or serve observations to the RCS Registrar; a re-examination is completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties by private written deed or civil-law notary of the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in French, German or English setting out the corporate general partner, limited partners, profit-share, management powers and Luxembourg registered-office address. Execute by private written deed; instruct a Luxembourg notary only where the SCSp receives contributions of immovable property or real rights therein (notarial deed mandatory) or if commercial counterparties require a notarized statute. Obtain the landlord's written consent for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certified identification and corporate documents of the general partner
Landlord's consent letter for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or notary identifies incomplete statutory content, execute a rectification deed or re-execute the partnership agreement; missing exhibits can be cured via a supplementary written rider signed by all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the capital contribution escrow account and deposit of subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution supervised by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the partnership's formation name at a licensed bank, collect each partner's subscription by SWIFT wire or local transfer, and obtain a banker's confirmation identifying each contributor and the amounts received. No statutory minimum applies, but the bank confirmation must evidence the contractually agreed capital before filing.
required_dossiers: KYC and AML documentation of each partner and ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a KYC query, provide source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership evidence promptly; if the bank refuses opening, substitute another licensed Luxembourg bank and restart the deposit without resubmitting the whole formation file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS incorporation filing through eJustice and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – eJustice electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership agreement, appointment of day-to-day manager, declaration of the registered office and the RCS registration application in the eJustice portal. Pay the electronic filing fee. After registration, the RCS publishes the formation data in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA); the SCSp is constituted on the registration and, if so elected in the partnership agreement, obtains legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Letter of appointment/acceptance by the day-to-day manager
Identity documents of partners and officers
Proof of registered office (lease or landlord consent)
eJustice RCS application form and fee proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rectification request, lodge the corrective set of documents through eJustice within the granted grace period; refile the corporate file which is then re-examined within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business identification, EORI and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Guichet.lu single window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of RCS registration, apply for the national business number and VAT number via the Guichet.lu portal, file the initial VAT declaration form as directed by the AEDT, and activate the EORI registration of the entity for all customs declarations connected with the bonded warehouse operation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If processing is delayed, file a written reminder via Guichet.lu and escalate to the AEDT enterprise desk; any incorrect VAT number is corrected by re-submission of the Form 102 online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs bonded-warehouse authorization for the free-trade-zone depot
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des douanes et accises du Luxembourg (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration) – Authorizations Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge an electronic authorization request under Articles 233 and 240 to 243 of the Union Customs Code for the operation of a customs warehouse or bonded depot in the free-trade-zone. Present the site layout, the electronic stock-account system, security and access-control arrangements, and a bank guarantee or cautionnement covering the customs debt at risk. The authorization is to be granted in the name of the registered SCSp.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorization is queried or provisionally refused, submit written observations within 10 business days with technically supplemented compliance evidence; lodge an administrative appeal before the Director of Customs if the refusal stands.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, fire-safety and occupational clearance for the physical depot
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement; Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the depot under the Law of 9 June 1999 on classified establishments and obtain the applicable class 2 or class 3 authorization from the Environment Agency and the commune. Have the fire-load and escape-plan dossier certified by the CGDIS; obtain a structural load-bearing certificate for racking and mezzanines; file with ITM the occupational-risk assessment and the workplace opening declaration.
required_dossiers: Fire-safety dossier with escape plan and extinguishing system data
Occupational health and safety risk assessment
Emergency response plan and waste-management docket
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon inspector observations, submit an amended technical dossier and request an on-site inspection appointment; temporary refusal is cured by full compliance and re-inspection before the warehouse commences operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Administration des douanes et accises du Luxembourg (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration) – Customs Authorizations and Bonded Warehouse Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Warehouse Authorization (autorisation d'entrepôt douanier) / Bonded Depot License in a Free Trade Zone under Articles 233 and 240–243 of the Union Customs Code

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg (Luxembourg Environment Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment (établissement classé) under the Law of 9 June 1999 – storage and depot activity normally rated Class 3 (communal authorization) or Class 2 (ministerial authorization) depending on tonnage and hazardous-goods thresholds; a full EIA report is not required for a standard bonded warehouse, but a prior environmental notification/screening is compulsory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge within communal sewer parameter limits (COD, BOD5, TSS, pH) and Grand-Ducal Regulation thresholds; VOC and combustion-emission ceilings per the transposed Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU; waste handling, traceability manifests and disposal obligations under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from CGDIS on fire load, escape routes and extinguishing installations; structural load-bearing inspection certificate for racking and storage platforms; occupational workplace clearance from ITM covering accident prevention, ventilation and workplace ergonomics.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Direct Tax Authority) and Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines / Administration de la TVA (VAT Authority) — Luxembourg; unified e-portal MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entities without a fixed establishment (including SCSp) must register for VAT via the MyGuichet.lu e-portal (form 645/646) before supplying taxable goods/services in Luxembourg or engaged in intra-EU/direct exports. A national business registration number (numéro national) or, for non-residents, a temporary VAT number is issued on a ‘VAT-on-demand’ basis, normally within 2–5 business days, upon submission of the partnership deed, director/manager identification, and a statement of intended activities. For TIN (income tax) purposes, non-resident partners must file Luxembourg tax returns; the SCSp itself is transparent and does not obtain a separate income tax ID, except for registration for withholding tax procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no ‘check-the-box’ election. An SCSp is statutorily transparent for corporate income tax and net wealth tax; it may, however, elect to be treated as a separate VAT registered person (assujetti distinct) for value added tax purposes. Under ATAD/anti-hybrid rules, the SCSp may opt to designate its transparent status for Luxembourg purposes; the partners must align classification with treaty and EU hybrid mismatch rules to avoid disallowance or double-deduction outcomes. No other fiscal elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for Luxembourg-established small enterprises; for non-residents supplying goods/services in Luxembourg or importing, registration is required regardless of threshold, and for intra-Community distance selling the EUR 35,000 threshold applies per country.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance (CTC) or mandatory digital stamping regime is in force in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing is permitted under EU Directive 2014/55 and Luxembourg VAT law, subject to authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and readability. B2B EDI or Peppol format (EN 16931) may be used. Cross-border B2B transactions require compliance with the EU CESOP reporting of payment data; from 1 January 2026, domestic B2B e-invoicing obligations will be phased in (Law of 15 July 2021 as amended). Until the mandate, paper or e-bills are equally accepted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to: (a) dispatches of goods to destinations outside the European Union, provided the goods are physically exported from Luxembourg or from another EU Member State by the seller or on its behalf; (b) supplies of goods dispatched to another EU Member State (intra-Community supply) if the tax ID of the recipient is valid; (c) services directly related to the export of goods (handling, transport, loading) and certain offshore services. The SCSp, if VAT-registered, may rely on the buyer’s EU VAT number or customs documentation to substantiate the export. Goods stored in a customs free zone/bonded depot qualify for zero-rating upon actual removal to a third country, subject to delivery and documentary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/Déclaration d'exportation with customs office stamp or AES electronic confirmation)
Bill of Lading / Airwaybill / CMR (transport contract evidencing physical movement)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of payment received in foreign currency from the export sale)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT Administration can retrospectively disallow zero-rating if export evidence is incomplete or forged. Reclaimed VAT or refunds are clawed back with default interest (0.8% per month) and penalties of 10% up to 200% of evaded VAT for negligent or intentional infringement, plus fines under the General Tax Code (Abgabenordnung) of up to EUR 250,000 for documentary fraud. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment for repeat fraudulent schemes. The standard control period is five years from the invoice due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as a Eurosystem member, with prudential oversight of credit institutions delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and customs/fiscal control assigned to the Administration des douanes et accises.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under TFEU Article 63 and Eurosystem statutes. The SCSp may freely receive equity contributions in EUR or foreign currency, hold multi-currency accounts, and remit profits, dividends, or liquidation proceeds without prior exchange-control authorization. The only administrative obligations are (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border flows exceeding EUR 12,500 and (ii) RBE beneficial-ownership registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers. No capital controls, ring-fencing, or minimum onshore retention periods apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or onshore-repatriation timeline for export receipts. Proceeds from bonded warehouse services and FTZ re-export may be retained indefinitely in the original settlement currency or converted at the operator's discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for principal treasury or clearing functions. Offshore digital EMIs without a full EU/EEA credit-institution licence or PSD2/EMD passporting cannot offer SWIFT MT103/MT700 settlement, T2 euro clearing, or commercial LC issuance. A licensed EEA EMI may serve only as an auxiliary non-bank channel for small-value disbursements and must not replace a CSSF-regulated credit institution for the SCSp's core accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one general-partner representative (natural person) and, when requested, the designated AML compliance officer of the SCSp must attend either (i) an in-person interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises or (ii) a CSSF-compliant remote video KYC session using an eIDAS-qualified electronic identification scheme, supplemented by a physical AML file delivered by courier. Fully remote opening is generally not permitted for a non-legal-personality partnership unless the bank holds a prior relationship with the general partner and the paper evidence pack is complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacks separate legal personality; banks must look through to the general partner and each limited partner with a 25% or greater economic interest for UBO identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) of the SCSp; current RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract; official Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) filing excerpt; organisational chart covering the full ownership chain; passport and proof-of-residence of the GP legal representative and all identified UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded warehouse activity in a free trade zone triggers customs-licence vetting; the bank may flag unlicensed customs warehousing or absence of an authorised economic operator where excise duties can attach.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid customs warehousing authorisation issued under Union Customs Code Article 240 by the Administration des douanes et accises; lease deed or ownership deed for premises located in the recognised Luxembourg free trade zone / free port; standard operating procedures for bonded inventory control; customs guarantee certificate or banker's bond covering posted duty liabilities; specimen INS-2 bonded inventory record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Medium-Risk-Enhanced rating for ISIC 5210 may trigger enhanced due diligence on source of funds and the supplier or tenant counterparty base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or bank-reviewed 24-month financial projections; independent source-of-wealth statement for each UBO supported by sale deeds, audited group financial statements, or fund redemption reports; counterparty KYC pack (licence, tax ID, beneficial owner list) for the top ten tenants and clients of the bonded depot; sanctions and PEP screening output from a reputable compliance provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipated high-volume FTZ trade flows could be mischaracterised as unlicensed money transmission or value-transfer services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Luxembourg-qualified law firm confirming that bonded warehouse storage, handling, and incidental logistics services do not constitute payment services, e-money issuance, or money remittance under the Luxembourg law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended by the law of 14 March 2018 (PSD2 transposition); physical facility inspection report; internal control manual demonstrating that warehouse fee invoicing and trade settlement are effected on the SCSp's own account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions route by SWIFT MT103 single credit transfer to the beneficiary account IBAN held at the selected tier-1 Luxembourg bank. The payment must identify the SCSp as beneficiary, reference the subscription or capital-injection instrument, and carry the ECB balance-of-payments classification code for partnership equity. EEA investors settle in EUR via Target2 (T2 dedicated cash account); non-EEA investors remit through the receiving bank's USD, CNY, or CHF correspondent (e.g., CHIPS/Fedwire, CIPS) and must append the intermediary BIC on the MT103. Verification requires a copy of the GP resolution, an updated register of contributions, and a simplified source-of-funds certificate for any single injection above EUR 100,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury settlements use SWIFT MT103 for supplier, storage-fee, and duty payments, and SWIFT MT700 (documentary letter of credit) for procurement or customs-guarantee transactions. EUR-denominated SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) settle same day in Target2; non-EUR disbursements clear via the correspondent banking network (USD via CHIPS/Fedwire, GBP via CHAPS, CNY via CIPS with Bank of China Luxembourg as intermediary). The SCSp should maintain a dedicated T2 liquidity buffer covering at least one month of customs-duty peaks and should, where trade volumes justify, open a CIPS/RMB clearing channel to support bonded re-export flows to Asia.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF FX forwards (standard 1M-12M tenor, extendable to 24M) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with an investment-grade Luxembourg or EU bank counterparty; EMIR trade-reporting obligations apply.
EUR/USD cross-currency basis swaps for hedging long-term USD-denominated warehouse assets or committed capital injections from non-EEA partners.
FX swaps (swap de change) for T+2 or intraday rolling conversion of large USD/CHF receipts into EUR to support customs-guarantee top-ups.

NDFs permissible only against restricted, non-convertible counterparty currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) arising from bonded re-export transactions, and only when documented as hedge instruments for commercially committed trade flows; NDFs on EUR are not market standard given full euro convertibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) of the SCSp, if required by size thresholds or by the partnership agreement/fund authorization, filed in RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end if the statutory reporting obligation applies (e.g., 31 July after a 31 December year-end); one month after approval if the general meeting is held later.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing reminder, administrative fine up to EUR 5,000, compulsory filing by court order, and eventual ex officio deregistration from the RCS if default continues.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE beneficial-owner confirmation (confirmation annuelle du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, generally by 31 March as announced by Luxembourg Business Registers; updates must be filed within one month of any transfer of SCSp partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 per infringement (or up to EUR 12,500 in aggravating circumstances), publication of default, and blocking of RCS-RBE filing services for the SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual bonded warehouse stock inventory report and customs stock records certification for the authorized customs warehouse/free trade zone depot
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Douanes et Accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the customs authorization or as fixed in the authorization; annual stocktake report to be submitted within 30 days after the authorized stocktake date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of duty-suspension status, immediate customs debt assessment on undeclared or discrepant goods, drawdown of the customs guarantee, suspension or revocation of the bonded warehouse authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg partnership income tax information declaration (déclaration collective) covering SCSp results and partner allocations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December of the year following the tax year; electronic filing extensions granted to 30 April of the subsequent year apply when the declaration is filed through MyGuichet.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty generally 10% of assessed tax after formal demand, continued default triggering a mandatory tax assessment, interest on arrears, and penalties against the general partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate records audit and update of RCS extract for general partner identity, registered office, and registered agent (if changed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS; minutes and registers kept at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each relevant corporate event; no separate annual RCS re-filing is due if no event occurred, but full regard must be paid to the annual RBE confirmation and minutes book verification.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS entry inconsistencies expose the general partner to civil liability and third-party reliance claims; administrative fines of up to EUR 1,000 may be imposed for incomplete register maintenance under Luxembourg commercial law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises is mandatory when the SCSp exceeds two of the three Luxembourg size thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, average headcount above 50. A CSSF-regulated SCSp (including a reserved alternative investment fund) is audited regardless of size; the partnership agreement may also require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2020 and the Luxembourg commercial code; IFRS as adopted by the EU applies to consolidated financial statements or funds whose constitutional documents, AIFM, or CSSF require fair-value/NAV reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an RBE file identifying all beneficial owners by holding percentage and control nature, confirm that file annually (generally by 31 March), and update it within one month of any transfer of partnership interests, contribution or liquidation event. A transfer is effective vis-à-vis the RCS/RBE only after the validated update; the general partner bears responsibility for complete, accurate, and timely confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Register of SCSp Partnership Interests)
Register of General Partner and Manager Decisions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline CIT for Luxembourg City (2024: 17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); reduced to 23.94% if 2025 rate cut to 16% is enacted; effective 15% CIT band up to EUR 175,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent: no CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at fund level; partners taxed at their own residence (EU-PSD/ATAD CFC caveats); free-zone bonded warehouse profits benefit from suspension of customs duties/VAT and deferral of recognition until distribution; participation exemption on subsequent dividends/capital gains at corporate-partner level; R&D tax credit 20%-44%; IP tax regime (if active) — now repealed for new IP from 2021, grandfathering until 2024; no WHT on distributions given transparency
